issues.description: The dark underlined number reads 16. The main heading reads Sigma_J et Sigma_{J,L}, followed by a stop. Several diagonal marginal fragments cross the heading and are clipped by this shallow box; their connected reading is in B02, rather than being completed from off-box letters in B01.

The slanted note is the connected in-scope text. Read point de vue, peut-être, plus commode, définir, éclatements, mieux adapté, formules, and the limit formula directly. The multi-index uses one short horizontal continuation rule between i_0 and i_n. The final upper Sigma has a raised L. Dans ce is partly overlapped. In et non Sigma_i subset X_i-star, the Sigma is heavily retraced or locally canceled; both states remain possible. In the final difference formula the last Sigma decoration cannot be separated securely from the i of the preceding line, hence dot/plain uncertainty. No mathematical identity check was performed.

The box also contains the already covered underlined 16, a clipped portion of the main heading, and incomplete background prefixes of the main Soit J une bande line and formula (70). Those are not independently completed in this marginal-note row; the complete heading is B01 and the complete displayed formula is B03. The lower edge clips the neighboring NB On a posé note, read as a connected note in B05. Cropped contextual fragments are not supplied as complete prose.

The relation in the upper line is subset. Below it are two vertical equality strokes. The first set-difference position has a dark triangular return and is retained as setminus versus greater-than uncertainty. T has a hollow circle above its bar. In the discarded lower-left union expression, the initial sign is obscured; union, j in J and Sigma_j remain recoverable. Two overwritten superscript sites in the following lower expression are treated as canceled doubtful stars; only those superscript sites, not the exposed X_J letters, are marked deleted. The NB has an underline. Several marginal fragments enter at the upper and left boundaries; B02/B05 give their connected readings.

Engendré is written across two lines, engen / dré. The first line reaches the dark right edge; the surviving letters with the following dré support the complete word. No missing terminal punctuation is supplied. The final relation has a lower bar, read less-than-or-equal.

On a posé is read from the tall initial p, reduced middle letters and detached acute. In the last relation the two equality strokes are clear, but a tall curly crossing stroke may be a not-equal cancellation or an attached question-like mark. Neither a clean equality nor a normalized identity is asserted. The parenthetical union is indexed j in bar J. Earlier marginal prose along the upper boundary is clipped context from B02.

Both empty-set-shaped glyphs have a loop and descending stem and are recorded as phi. The second line literally has si J un idéal, without an inserted est. The left brace groups the two lines and has no matching right brace.

Read On trouve, sauf erreur. The initial part of trouve is crossed by the slanted marginal note, but the tall t and following connected r/o/u/v/e strokes support trouve. No final stop is visible in this box. Clipped marginal fragments are read in B09.

The first member of the parenthesized list is Sigma_j and the second Sigma_ij. Before the inner opening parenthesis a canceled b-like glyph remains doubtful. The operator-label subscripts cannot be segmented securely between j and ij; both choices are retained locally. The two right-going shafts end with small turned/looped returns, rather than separately visible triangular chevrons; their observed geometry is drawn without generic arrowheads. The upper limit underline has a clear right arrowhead; the second limit has only a plain underline. There are two openings before the diagram but only one visible right closure; no extra closure is supplied. The discarded line along the bottom is repeated in B10 because it belongs to both rectangles.

The note begins NB Sigma_J est muni d’une and continues with a long stratification-like word crossed by the main text. The following word favors quelconque, but que plus an obscured word remains possible. The short word before the tuple is not secure between avec and aux. The tuple letters and jh indices are independently read; the fourth coefficient is b. The terminal quantifier has an angular universal shape followed by h in I. Some punctuation around the wrapped clauses is weak. The main-text On trouve, formula numbers (72)/(73), canceled phrase, and On pose enter this broad margin rectangle as clipped background; connected main-text readings appear in B07/B08/B10/B11/B12 and are not completed off-box in this marginal row.

Par suite is readable beneath a long cancellation stroke. The next tall right-angled form may be L or a perpendicular sign; the final compact wavy ink cannot be segmented as a secure word and is left illegible. The whole line, including the trailing forms, is canceled. The unresolved tail may include an aborted mathematical stroke rather than a completed lexical word.

The arrow has a plain curled tail and a distinct right arrowhead. A small h stands above a separate tilde. The right parenthetical phrase wraps homo- / topie; the visible terminal dash is preserved, and no punctuation outside the rectangle is supplied.

Sigma_J has a distinct solid dot. The X_J has two tiny detached specks near its upper-right arm, which do not form a secure star; X_J is the independent reading, with the specks documented here instead of silently upgraded to an asterisk. The annotation under T has a flat bracket with upturned ends, encoded underbracket, and its union index uses a short horizontal minus between bar J and J, whereas the main T subscript uses an oblique setminus. The first letter of Im is retraced but readable. The source of the following map has ij, including a short i and long j. The final condition reads d in Drap, d avec au moins 2 termes; no (J) argument is supplied. The black bottom edge touches some low strokes; no additional off-edge text or punctuation is reconstructed.
